title: Street Parking Meter Overlay Sticker

scenario.context: You park your car in downtown. On the metallic parking meter, a freshly printed sticker covers the original payment instructions: 'Quick Pay by QR Code — Scan to Avoid $50 Citation'.

options.text: SAFE — Convenient modern contactless municipal payment
SUSPICIOUS — Verify whether physical sticker is pasted over the original meter and pay via official meter keypad/app
MALICIOUS — Physical QR sticker overlay harvesting credit cards on generic .online domain

indicators.description: Adhesive sticker placed over official municipal parking hardware
Unofficial '.online' domain rather than municipal government '.gov'
Threat of immediate $50 citation to rush payment decision

explanation: Criminals paste malicious QR stickers over legitimate parking meters across major cities. Scanning the code opens a fake payment portal that steals credit card numbers while victims still get ticketed because parking was never paid.
hints: Is the QR code physically printed onto the machine itself or is it an adhesive sticker slapped on top?
Does the URL domain end with an official city .gov or a private .online extension?
Can you pay using the official municipal parking app or physical coin/card slot instead?
learningObjective: Inspect physical QR code surfaces for sticker overlays and verify domain authenticity.
consequenceChain: You scanned the overlaid sticker and entered credit card details
Card details saved to fraudster's database and sold online
Parking authority issued $50 ticket because parking was never actually registered
recoverySteps: Report compromised parking meter to city parking enforcement
Cancel and replace the credit card used on the fraudulent portal
Dispute unauthorized recurring charges

title: Restaurant Table Digital Menu & 50% Coupon

scenario.context: At a crowded café, a loose printed acrylic card on your table reads: 'Scan for Full Digital Menu + Get Instant 50% OFF Your Bill!'.

options.text: SAFE — Great restaurant promotion
SUSPICIOUS — Ask waiter for physical menu and avoid downloading third-party APKs
MALICIOUS — Android malware / APK installer disguised as a discount coupon

indicators.description: Attempts to download executable APK file rather than displaying a web menu
50% discount used as psychological bait to compromise smartphone
Third-party generic .info APK download site

explanation: QR codes that prompt you to download or install an application (especially .APK files on Android or configuration profiles on iOS) are almost always Trojan malware. Menus and coupons only require standard web pages.
hints: Why would a restaurant menu require installing an APK application file?
Does viewing a menu ever require downloading executable software?
Always inspect the destination before accepting any device download prompts.
learningObjective: Never install application files (.apk, .mobileconfig) prompted by QR codes.
consequenceChain: You scanned QR and tapped 'Install APK anyway'
Banking trojan installed in background with Accessibility permissions
Trojan recorded banking credentials and intercepted SMS OTPs
recoverySteps: Boot phone into Safe Mode and uninstall rogue application
Revoke Device Admin and Accessibility Service permissions
Factory reset smartphone if deep persistence was established

title: University Campus Student Event Flyer

scenario.context: A poster pinned to the student union bulletin board advertises: 'Campus Spring Gala 2024 — Free Pizza & Concert Tickets! Scan QR code to log into Student Portal and RSVP'.

options.text: SAFE — Standard university student club poster
SUSPICIOUS — Check university student activities website independently
MALICIOUS — Phishing portal on .xyz domain harvesting campus SSO credentials

indicators.description: Mimics campus event to harvest student and faculty university credentials
Unofficial '.xyz' domain instead of university '.edu'
Free food and tickets used to lower student vigilance

explanation: Anyone with a printer can pin flyers to open public bulletin boards. Campus phishing via QR codes exploits trust in university branding to steal .edu email credentials and tuition payment portals.
hints: Check if the URL ends in your university's legitimate '.edu' domain.
Can anyone pin posters to a public campus bulletin board?
Log into your student portal via your bookmarked campus URL instead.
learningObjective: Recognize campus bulletin board quishing targeting higher education credentials.
consequenceChain: You submitted campus SSO credentials on the fake login page
Attacker logged into student portal and changed tuition refund bank account
Stolen .edu address used to blast internal phishing emails across the student directory
recoverySteps: Alert Campus Information Security / IT Helpdesk
Reset university single-sign-on password immediately
Verify direct deposit financial aid routing details

title: Delivery Notice Tag Attached to Front Door

scenario.context: You find a yellow card clipped to your apartment door: 'Missed Package Delivery #8921. Driver unable to access gate. Scan QR to pay $2.50 redelivery fee and confirm address'.

options.text: SAFE — Normal courier missed delivery card
SUSPICIOUS — Contact your building management or use the tracking number on official carrier app
MALICIOUS — Physical doorstep scam collecting payment cards and residential occupancy patterns

indicators.description: Physical flyer placed on door to create high perceived legitimacy
Shady '.cc' top-level domain
Small fee ($2.50) designed to extract credit card details effortlessly

explanation: Criminals blanket entire apartment complexes with fake missed delivery notices. The physical touchpoint builds instant credibility, but the QR code routes to an off-brand payment harvester.
hints: Look at the domain extension in the QR destination preview (.cc).
Does the card name a recognized postal or courier carrier?
Always track packages by typing the tracking code directly on the official postal website.
learningObjective: Identify physical doorstep delivery card scams and resist impulse fee payments.
consequenceChain: You scanned QR and entered credit card details for $2.50 redelivery
Card details recorded and charged for unauthorized international retail purchases
No package ever existed
recoverySteps: Alert apartment building management about unauthorized door solicitations
Freeze compromised payment card and file bank fraud dispute
Warn neighbors about the scam notices

title: Electric Scooter QR Code Unlock Tamper

scenario.context: You want to rent a shared electric scooter on the sidewalk. You notice the QR code between the handlebars looks slightly raised and misaligned compared to the scooter's factory paint.

options.text: SAFE — Standard scooter unlock code
SUSPICIOUS — Use the scooter ID number inside the official pre-installed app instead of scanning the camera code
MALICIOUS — Physical sticker replacement redirecting riders to fake billing portal

indicators.description: Raised and misaligned sticker covering the manufacturer's laser-etched QR code
Generic website destination instead of deep-linking into the verified mobile app
Bypasses mobile OS verified app link handler

explanation: Scammers replace laser-etched QR codes on shared mobility scooters and bikes with adhesive stickers. Scanning them opens a fake unlock site rather than triggering the official mobile app's in-app handler.
hints: Feel the edges of the QR code — is it a sticker pasted over the original surface?
Why did the QR code open a browser web page instead of opening your installed scooter app?
Most rental apps let you manually type in the scooter's visible numeric vehicle ID.
learningObjective: Differentiate between genuine in-app deep-linking QR codes and malicious browser redirects.
consequenceChain: You scanned the counterfeit sticker and entered card info on the website
The scooter never unlocked because the real rental service received no command
Attacker obtained credit card data while you were left stranded
recoverySteps: Report vandalized vehicle number to mobility company support
Cancel payment card through your bank app
Only unlock mobility vehicles using in-app numeric entry

title: Airport Wi-Fi Connect QR Code

scenario.context: At an international airport departure lounge, a flyer on the seating table displays: 'Fast Free 5G Airport Wi-Fi — Scan QR to Connect Instantly'. Scanning prompts your phone to download an iOS Mobile Configuration Profile / Android VPN Profile.

options.text: SAFE — Standard profile installation required for enterprise airport Wi-Fi certificates
SUSPICIOUS — Wi-Fi networks should not require installing root configuration profiles or private VPN profiles
MALICIOUS — Rogue configuration profile installing malicious root CA certificate to decrypt SSL traffic (MITM)

indicators.description: Prompts installation of .mobileconfig containing rogue root certificate authority
Rogue root certificate allows attackers to perform SSL decryption on all encrypted traffic

explanation: Never install configuration profiles (.mobileconfig) or root certificates from public QR codes. A rogue root certificate grants the attacker full capability to intercept, inspect, and decrypt your HTTPS banking and email traffic in real time.
hints: Does standard public Wi-Fi ever require installing an iOS Configuration Profile in Device Settings?
What happens when a device trusts an unknown root Certificate Authority?
Connect to Wi-Fi exclusively via your phone's native Settings menu.
learningObjective: Understand the severe dangers of malicious configuration profiles and rogue root certificates.
consequenceChain: You installed the profile in phone Settings and trusted the root certificate
Attacker's rogue gateway decrypted your HTTPS banking sessions
All login passwords and private messages intercepted in cleartext
recoverySteps: Go to phone Settings -> General -> VPN & Device Management and delete the rogue profile immediately
Rotate all passwords entered while connected to the rogue network
Use cellular roaming or trusted personal VPN hotspot instead

title: Crypto ATM Bitcoin Deposit QR Code Swap

scenario.context: A caller claiming to be from the Federal Trade Commission instructs you: 'Your bank account is compromised. Transfer your savings to a Federal Reserve Protected Bitcoin Locker by scanning this QR code at any cryptocurrency kiosk'.

options.text: SAFE — Government-backed protective escrow account
SUSPICIOUS — Verify directly with local bank branch
MALICIOUS — 100% scam; government agencies never demand cryptocurrency deposits or Bitcoin ATM transfers

indicators.description: No government or law enforcement agency uses Bitcoin ATMs or crypto lockers
Cryptocurrency blockchain transactions are mathematically irreversible once confirmed
Impersonates Federal Trade Commission / law enforcement to compel panic

explanation: No legitimate government entity, police department, IRS agent, or utility company will ever instruct you to deposit cash into a Bitcoin ATM or scan a crypto QR code. Cryptocurrency transactions are irreversible.
hints: Do federal agencies maintain Bitcoin ATM safety lockers?
Can cryptocurrency blockchain transfers be refunded if you get scammed?
Hang up immediately on anyone directing you toward a cryptocurrency kiosk.
learningObjective: Recognize cryptocurrency ATM transfer coercion schemes and understand blockchain irreversibility.
consequenceChain: You fed cash into the Bitcoin ATM and scanned the attacker's wallet QR code
Bitcoin transferred immediately to attacker's non-custodial wallet
Transactions were irreversibly confirmed on blockchain with zero recourse
recoverySteps: Terminate all communication with the caller immediately
File a report with the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3.gov)
Contact local police department financial crimes division

title: Cross-Device QR Login Hijacking (QRLJacking)

scenario.context: You visit a web page claiming to offer a $100 gift card if you link your Discord/WhatsApp/Telegram account. The page displays a 'Scan QR code in your mobile app to link account and claim reward'.

options.text: SAFE — The QR code uses official domain (discord.com)
SUSPICIOUS — Verify whether scanning logs a new desktop session on your personal account
MALICIOUS — QRLJacking attack; scanning grants the attacker's browser full login session access to your account

indicators.description: Attacker proxies the service's official QR login code onto a phishing page
Scanning authorizes the attacker's remote web browser as a logged-in device
Gift card incentive tricks user into approving device pairing prompt

explanation: QRLJacking (QR Login Hijacking) occurs when an attacker requests a legitimate login QR code from Discord/WhatsApp/Telegram and embeds it onto a fake reward page. When you scan it with your phone, you approve the attacker's computer to log into your account!
hints: What does scanning a QR code inside WhatsApp or Discord settings actually do?
Does scanning link a new computer to your account?
Never scan in-app login QR codes displayed on third-party promotional websites.
learningObjective: Understand QRLJacking (QR Login Hijacking) and never scan in-app device pairing codes on untrusted websites.
consequenceChain: You scanned the QR code using your messaging app camera
Attacker's browser session instantly logged into your account
Attacker downloaded your private chat history and messaged your contacts asking for emergency money
recoverySteps: Open messaging app settings -> Linked Devices -> Log out of ALL unknown sessions immediately
Enable account PIN / 2FA passcode
Warn friends that recent messages from your account were sent by a malicious intruder
